correctness.rationale: For t∈[0,1], with M=#{i:|U_i|>t}, direct octahedral incidence gives M(5−M) crossing edges, whence M0=empty, M1=quadrilateral, M2/3=hexagon, except null tangencies. Let a1=1−t, a2=P(|U1|>t,|U2|>t), a3=P(all3>t). Conditional uniformity on coordinate circles derives a2′=−2+4θ/π for t<1/√2, a3′=−3+12θ/π for t<1/√3, θ=asin(t/sqrt(1−t²)), with respective initial values1; J′=θ and J0=0 give exact a2,a3. Inclusion–exclusion yields three stated branches and endpoints. The quad derivative is 12θ/π below 1/√3, 9−24θ/π between the thresholds, −3 above1/√2; θ increases strictly, giving unique θ=3π/8, t*=0.678598344545847. Independently numerically recomputed exact phase probabilities at t=0,1/√3,0.6,t*, plus normalization and max 0.9066856793387306 using high precision. The bound t=1 gives empty section generically, and t0 gives hexagon. Finite numerical checks corroborate the all-offset analytic proof, not replace it.
